title: Item 17a · How money is written (and how names are listed)
subtitle: Approved in each section. Money is written two ways: whole dollars on the rosters and in Camps (“$790”, “Paid $160”, “$375”) with cents only when there are some (Black Belt can take “$290.50”), and always with cents in Finance (“$245.00”). Five separate helpers do this; Star's would write $32.50 as “$32.5” — hidden today because Star only takes whole dollars. Names are listed three ways, each approved for a reason: testing rosters by belt, then last name; Camps' roster by first name (v0.715 — campers are called by first name); Prospects and Calendar as “Ava R.” (privacy, v0.245). Already settled in item 3: “Paid by” everywhere (Black Belt's “Method” goes); “Paying by” stays for the family's choice before paying. (Preview screenshots at PC size · fake data)

items.caption: 1. Star (Color Belt, Black Belt and Camps the same): whole dollars — “$790”, “Paid $160”.
2. Camps: “5 to collect · $375”; its roster is A–Z by first name (v0.715).
3. Finance: always cents — “$245.00”, “$140.00” — amounts are counted against the drawer and line up in columns.

columns.label: Option C drawn · option B changes nothing on screen

items.caption: 4. Option C — cents everywhere: “$790.00”, “Paid $160.00” — the warning drops to a second line and roster rows get longer (worse on a phone).

columns.note: Option B (recommended) changes nothing on screen. It writes today's practice down as the rule — on screens, whole dollars (“$65”), cents only when there are some (“$290.50”); in Finance's report, print and export, always cents (“$65.00”). Behind the scenes the five money helpers become one, so no section can drift (Star's “$32.5”). Names stay as approved and go into the same rule: testing rosters by belt, then last name; Camps by first name; Prospects and Calendar “Ava R.”. Picture 4 is drawn over the real Star roster; nothing in the app was changed.

footer:
Your choice — one question: how should money be written?
A · Keep as today. + no work. − no written rule, so a new screen can pick a third style; five helpers can drift (Star's “$32.5”).
B · Recommended: write today's practice down as the rule, with one shared money helper. Screens: “$65”, cents only when there are some; Finance's report, print and export: “$65.00”. Names stay as they are, in the same rule. + nothing changes on screen; the rule stops drift. − a small behind-the-scenes job (one helper instead of five).
C · Cents everywhere (picture 4). + one style, like a receipt book. − every roster, card and tag gets longer; warnings wrap to a second line, worse on phones.
